facts.statement: An incomplete skull and nearly complete lower jaw were discovered in 1971 near Shar Tsav, Mongolia, during a Soviet-Mongolian expedition.
facts.quote: During the Combined Soviet-Mongolian Paleontological Expeditions in 1971, an isolated, incomplete sauropod skull and nearly complete mandible were unearthed at a fossil site in the Upper Cretaceous bluffs of the Barun Goyot Formation near Shar Tsav, Mongolia.

facts.statement: The genus name means "abnormal lizard" due to its strange skull, while the species name means "eastern" because the fossils came from Mongolia.
facts.quote: the genus name meaning "abnormal lizard" after the abnormal skull anatomy and the species name meaning "eastern", referring to the fossil's origin in Mongolia.

facts.statement: Quaesitosaurus is a genus of sauropod containing only one species, Q. orientalis, which means "extraordinary lizard".
facts.quote: Quaesitosaurus (meaning "extraordinary lizard") is a genus of nemegtosaurid sauropod containing only the type species, Q. orientalis, described in 1983.

facts.statement: Its long, low, horse-like skull with peg-teeth resembles that of Diplodocus, leading to speculation that its body was also diplodocid-like.
facts.quote: With long, low and horse-like with frontally located peg-teeth, the skull of Quaesitosaurus is similar enough to the skull of Diplodocus and its kin to have prompted informed speculation that the missing body was built like those of diplodocids.

facts.statement: Based on related species, Quaesitosaurus is estimated to have been about 12 meters long.
facts.quote: Quaesitosaurus was a large-sized titanosaur, with an estimated length of about 12 m based on relatives.

facts.statement: The fossil evidence shows that the tooth crowns of Quaesitosaurus were long and thin.
facts.quote: The tooth crowns were long and thin.

facts.statement: Only one skull, catalogued as PIN 3906/2, is known, and it is very long and horse-like with pencil-like teeth.
facts.quote: Sólo se conoce un cráneo de Quaesitosaurus, PIN n.º 3906/2, siendo muy largo similar al de un caballo con dientes como lápices.

facts.statement: A notable feature is a channel in the basioccipital and basipterygoid leading from the pituitary gland to the region below the occipital condyle.
facts.quote: En este se destaca la presencia de un canal en el basioccipital y el basiefenoide que conducen de la hipófisis a la región debajo del cóndilo occipital.

facts.statement: The snout of Q. orientalis appears wider than in Nemegtosaurus, and the squamosal is shorter and does not contact the squamosal-jugal.
facts.quote: El hocico de Q. orientalis parece ser más amplio que en Nemegtosaurus y el escamoso más corto y no entra en contacto con el cuadrado-yugal.

facts.statement: Many skull parts like the dorsal processes of the maxillae, jugals, and lacrimals are missing, so the shapes of the nostril borders and anteorbital window remain hypothetical.
facts.quote: Los procesos dorsales de los maxilares y de los premaxilares son los que falta, al igual que los yugales, lacrimales, prefrontales, y parte del frontal, así que no se preserva ninguna parte de los bordes de las narinas o de la ventana anteorbital, y sus formas siguen siendo hipotéticas.

facts.statement: The lower jaw is essentially complete.
facts.quote: La mandíbula está esencialmente completa.

facts.statement: Originally, Quaesitosaurus was classified in Dicraeosauridae with Dicraeosaurus because it was one of the few sauropods with preserved skulls.
facts.quote: Classification When Quaesitosaurus was originally described, it was placed with the Jurassic African Dicraeosaurus in Dicraeosauridae because it was one of the few other sauropods with preserved skulls known.

facts.statement: Recent analysis has reclassified Quaesitosaurus into the family Nemegtosauridae alongside Nemegtosaurus.
facts.quote: However, recent analysis has placed Quaesitosaurus along with Nemegtosaurus in the Nemegtosauridae.

facts.statement: Quaesitosaurus belongs to the family Nemegtosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Nemegtosauridae

facts.statement: Quaesitosaurus lived between 72 and 71 million years ago in the Late Cretaceous within the Barun Goyot Formation.
facts.quote: It lived from 72 to 71 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous epoch in the Barun Goyot Formation.

facts.statement: The Barun Goyot Formation where it lived was deposited in alluvial, lacustrine, and aeolian environments under arid to semiarid climates.
facts.quote: The sediments of this formation were deposited in alluvial plain (flat land consisting of sediments deposited by highland rivers), lacustrine, and aeolian paleoenvironments, under relatively arid to semiarid climates.

facts.statement: It lived at the end of the Cretaceous, approximately 85 to 71 million years ago during the Campanian, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 85 y 71 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for Quaesitosaurus is estimated from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Nemegtosaurus is a very close relative of Quaesitosaurus or simply a variation of the same animal.
facts.quote: It is possible that Nemegtosaurus, also known from only skull material, is a very close relative of Quaesitosaurus.

facts.statement: Many differences originally used to distinguish Quaesitosaurus from Nemegtosaurus are now thought to be due to skull deformation and inadequate initial descriptions.
facts.quote: However, many of these differences are actually due to the deformation of the skull and an inadequate description, as later studies showed.

facts.statement: Researchers speculate that the missing body of Quaesitosaurus was built like that of diplodocids based on its skull.
facts.quote: informed speculation that the missing body was built like those of diplodocids.

facts.statement: Like Nemegtosaurus and Rapetosaurus, the skull of Quaesitosaurus was extended and fell forward, with nasal openings high at the level of the eye socket.
facts.quote: As with Nemegtosaurus and Rapetosaurus, the skull was extended and fell forward, with the nasal openings located high at the skull at the level of the eye socket.

facts.statement: A 2005 study by Wilson found unique characteristics in the skull that support Quaesitosaurus as a distinct genus separate from Nemegtosaurus.
facts.quote: Wilson (2005) published an extensive new description of the Nemegtosaurus skull and found further characteristics (autapomorphies) that support the status of its own genus for Quaesitosaurus.

facts.statement: Nemegtosaurus, known only from skull material, might be a close relative of Quaesitosaurus or actually just a variation of the same animal.
facts.quote: Es posible que Nemegtosaurus, también conocido solo por material craneal, sea o un familiar cercano de Quaesitosaurus, si no de hecho una variación del mismo animal.

rejected.statement: The genus was formally named Quaesitosaurus orientalis by Kurzanov and Bannikov in 1983.
rejected.quote: The specimen wasn't described until 1983, when S. M. Kurzanov and A. F. Bannikov named it Quaesitosaurus orientalis.
rejected.reason: quote not found verbatim in the source
